content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Your `/work` directory is empty, so we'll build from scratch. Before I start, a few quick questions to make sure I build the right thing:

1. **Platform** — What form should this take?
   - Web app (runs in browser, accessible anywhere)
   - CLI tool (terminal, fast for keyboard-driven workflows)
   - Browser extension (save the current tab with one click)
   - Desktop app

2. **Core features** — Which matter to you? (tags, folders, full-text search, auto-fetching page titles/favicons, importing existing browser bookmarks, notes per bookmark)

3. **Users** — Just you locally, or multi-user / hosted for others?

4. **Tech preference** — Any language/framework you want (or want to avoid)? Otherwise I'll pick something sensible.

If you'd rather I just make reasonable choices and go, say the word — my default would be a **local web app**: Python + FastAPI backend, SQLite storage, a clean single-page frontend, with tags, search, and auto-fetched titles/favicons. Easy to run locally and extend later.

content:
Everything works end-to-end. The app is built and verified.

## What I built

A local bookmarks manager — FastAPI + SQLite backend, vanilla-JS single-page frontend, no build step.

```
/work
├── app/
│   ├── main.py       # FastAPI app + REST API (CRUD, search, tags)
│   ├── db.py         # SQLite schema & connection
│   └── metadata.py   # URL normalization + title/favicon fetching
├── static/           # index.html, style.css, app.js (the UI)
├── tests/test_api.py # 6 passing smoke tests (no network needed)
├── requirements.txt
└── README.md
```

**Verified working:**
- ✅ 6/6 tests pass
- ✅ Server boots; frontend (`/`) and assets serve (200)
- ✅ Live create/list/search/tags round-trip — note the `POST "example.com"` came back with the scheme added (`https://example.com`), the auto-fetched title (`Example Domain`), and a favicon URL

**Features:** add by URL with auto-fetched title & favicon, tags (comma-separated, click to filter), live full-text search over title/URL/notes, per-bookmark notes, delete with automatic orphan-tag cleanup. Case-insensitive tags, and the DB path is overridable via `BOOKMARKS_DB`.

## Run it

```bash
cd /work
source .venv/bin/activate        # deps already installed
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

Then open **http://127.0.0.1:8000**.

A few things I deliberately left for later (noted in the README): inline editing in the UI (the `PUT` endpoint already backs it), importing browser bookmark exports, FTS5 search, and auth for hosted/multi-user use.

content:
Inline editing is done and verified.

**What I added** (frontend only — the `PUT` endpoint already existed):
- An **✎ edit** button on each card, alongside delete.
- Clicking it swaps the card into an inline form with editable **title**, **tags** (comma-separated), and **notes** — the URL stays shown but fixed, since it's the bookmark's identity.
- **Save** writes via `PUT` and refreshes; **Cancel** restores the read-only view with no request.

**Verified live:**
- ✅ `PUT` updated title → `New Title`, tags → `edited, new`, notes → `new notes`
- ✅ The orphaned `old` tag was auto-cleaned after the edit (tag list shows only `edited` and `new`)
- ✅ Served `app.js` includes the new edit code

Run it the same way (`uvicorn app.main:app --reload`, open http://127.0.0.1:8000) and you'll see the pencil icon on each bookmark.

content:
Browser-bookmark import is done and verified.

**What I added:**
- **`app/importer.py`** — a parser for the Netscape bookmark format that every browser exports (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge). It walks the nested `<DL>`/`<H3>` structure so folder names become tags (nested folders → multiple tags), and also reads Firefox's per-link `TAGS="..."` attribute.
- **`POST /api/import`** — accepts the file's HTML, dedupes against existing URLs, skips non-web links (`javascript:`, `place:`, `data:`), and returns `{imported, skipped}`. It uses titles from the file + the favicon service, skipping per-page fetches so a large import stays fast.
- **Import UI** in the sidebar — a file picker, a "Use folders as tags" toggle, and a status line reporting the result.

**Verified live** with a realistic export:
- ✅ 3 web links imported, 1 `javascript:` bookmarklet skipped
- ✅ Folder `News` became a tag on both news links; GitHub's explicit `TAGS="dev,code"` came through
- ✅ Re-importing the same file imports 0 (all deduped) — confirmed in tests
- ✅ 9/9 tests pass, including a case where `folders_as_tags: false` keeps explicit tags but drops folder tags

**One bug caught and fixed along the way:** `javascript:void(0)` was being imported because `normalize_url` blindly prepended `https://` to anything without `://`. The importer now checks the URL scheme *before* normalizing, so only real http(s) links get in.

To use it: run the app, click **Choose bookmarks file…** in the sidebar, and pick your browser's exported `.html`. (In most browsers: bookmarks manager → Export bookmarks to HTML.)

Want import to also de-duplicate against different-but-equivalent URLs (trailing slashes, `www.`), or should we move on to something else — FTS5 search, or auth for hosting?

content:
Full-text search is upgraded and verified.

**What changed:**
- **`bookmarks_fts` FTS5 index** (in `db.py`) over title, URL, description, and tags. It's kept in sync with the bookmarks table via a `_reindex()` helper called on every create, edit, delete, and import. There's also a one-time **backfill** so an existing pre-FTS database gets indexed automatically on next startup.
- **Search now uses `MATCH` + BM25 ranking** instead of `LIKE`. The query builder quotes each token (so punctuation can't break FTS syntax) and appends `*` for prefix matching; multiple words are AND-ed. Results come back relevance-ranked when searching, newest-first otherwise.

**Verified live:**
- ✅ **Prefix**: `pyth` matched all three Python-related bookmarks (including one that only mentions "python" in its notes)
- ✅ **Relevance ranking**: "Python Programming Language" (title hit) ranked above the description-only hits
- ✅ **Multi-word AND**: `python web` returned only Django (the one with both terms)
- ✅ **Tags searchable**: searching a tag word finds the bookmark (covered in tests)
- ✅ **Robust to punctuation**: `c++`, `"unterminated`, `foo:bar`, `*` all return 200 instead of FTS syntax errors
- ✅ **Backfill**: rows indexed correctly after simulating an upgrade from a pre-FTS DB
- ✅ **12/12 tests pass**

The search box behaves the same in the UI — it's just much smarter now. The two obvious remaining items are auth for hosting and smarter URL de-duplication (trailing slashes, `www.`). Want either of those, or is this a good place to pause?
Honestly this all sounds great — I think this is a good place to pause. Thanks for building it out!
